applies_why: The judge text is deciding a link collision involving the pressing side's own chain, so K-C's chain-against-chain/footing requirement governs.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'never verse by verse' — I weighed whether the judge compared the defender's depth-idiom chain with the challenger's Matthew/Galatians chain by footing, or instead rejected the point because a verse alone does not name the channel.
why: The judge treats the question as open because the text does not name whose body is the channel, which is a verse-level absence test rather than a chain-against-chain footing comparison.
